item.title: On the number of zeros of polyanalytic polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2611.13278v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a complex polynomial $f(z,\bar z)$ of degree $n$ in $z$ and degree $m<n$ in $\bar{z}$, with finitely many zeros, has at most $(4m+1)n-5m$ distinct zeros in $\mathbb{C}$. The proof uses an approach suggested by GPT-6.1 based on a topological result of Kronheimer and Mrowka (Thom's Conjecture). We provide examples showing that the bound is asymptotically sharp as $n\to\infty$ for each fixed $m$.
item.dc:creator: Erik Lundberg, Zvi Rosen, Teng Zhang

item.title: Sharp weighted Riesz inequalities for harmonic mappings in the range 1<p<2
item.description: arXiv:2611.13285v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $1<p<2$ and $c>0$, we determine the exact norm of the weighted analytic--coanalytic projection operator $F\mapsto(P_+F,\sqrt c\,P_-F)$ from $L^p(\T)$ to $L^p(\T;\ell_2^2)$. The sharp constant is \[ a_{p,c}=\left(\frac{1+c+\sqrt{1+c^2+2c\cos(2\pi/p)}}{2\sin^2(\pi/p)}\right)^{1/2}. \] We construct an explicit plurisubharmonic minorant of the corresponding pointwise obstacle and obtain an origin-corrected inequality for arbitrary harmonic decompositions. The uncorrected inequality holds under an optimal angular condition at the origin. The scalar estimate underlying the construction is proved by angular minimization and a two-sided comparison with solutions of $y''=y$. An explicit family establishes sharpness.
item.dc:creator: David Kalaj, Anton Gjokaj

item.title: Bounded point evaluations in spaces of several complex variables
item.description: arXiv:2611.13290v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The focus of this manuscript is existence criteria for bounded point evaluations and bounded point derivations. In the single variable setting conditions for the existence of bounded point evaluations and derivations are known for many spaces of functions; however, in the several variable case far less is known. In this manuscript, we consider Campanato spaces, which contain many other function spaces as special cases, and prove sufficient conditions for the existence of bounded point evaluations in these spaces that are analogs of known results for the single variable case. We also demonstrate that for certain cases these sufficient conditions are also necessary.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Deterding

item.title: Product Asymptotics for Rows of the Walsh Table on Regular Compact Sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.13409v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $E$ be a regular compact set with connected complement, and let $f$ be holomorphic in a neighborhood of $E$. We establish Hadamard-type asymptotic formulas for products of errors of best uniform rational approximation of $f$ on $E$, formed from the first $m+1$ rows of the Walsh table. When the corresponding meromorphy radii are finite, we also show that the extremal exponential rates of the approximation errors along these rows are attained along a common subsequence. We also prove a sharp asymptotic comparison theorem for ratios of best rational approximation errors along fixed rows of the Walsh table on $E$ and its closed Green sublevel sets, and derive corresponding sharp asymptotic estimates for ratios of their products. These results extend earlier product theorems from continua with connected complement and Jordan boundary to the more general setting of regular compact sets with connected complement.
item.dc:creator: V. A. Prokhorov

item.title: Quasisymmetric rigidity of self-similar square carpets
item.description: arXiv:2611.13725v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $S$ be a self-similar square carpet obtained by subdividing the unit square into $n^2$ congruent cells, deleting a nonempty collection of strictly interior open cells with pairwise disjoint closures, and repeating the same pattern with the same orientation in every retained cell. We prove that every quasisymmetric self-homeomorphism of $S$, equipped with the Euclidean metric, is a Euclidean isometry. The result holds for every integer $n\ge3$ and imposes no symmetry condition on the deletion pattern. Consequently, the quasisymmetric and isometric groups coincide with the stabilizer of the first-generation holes in the symmetry group of the square. The proof combines round uniformization and Schottky-map stabilization with a propagation argument across retained cells. This produces global homothety relations for conjugates of cell contractions and forces preservation of the outer peripheral square. Periodic points on its sides then yield preservation of the corners, reducing the conclusion to the four-corner rigidity theorem for square carpets.
item.dc:creator: Xiaohua Wang, Fan Wen

item.title: Newton non-degenerate holomorphic foliations and their separatrices
item.description: arXiv:2611.14466v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we study germs of holomorphic foliations in the complex plane that are Newton non-degenerate. This is an algebraic condition attached to the Newton polygon of the foliation, analogous to the one defined by Kouchnirenko for analytic curves and, more generally, hypersurfaces. As in this case, the condition of Newton non-degeneracy for foliations can be identified through the comparison of two numerical invariants: the Newton number - a computation involving simple geometric data of the Newton polygon - and the Milnor number. The Newton number is never greater than the Milnor number, and the foliation is Newton non-degenerate if and only if they are equal. The assumption that a foliation is Newton non-degenerate imposes conditions on its set of separatrices. We prove that, under this hypothesis, the foliation has no weak separatrices and, hence, all its separatrices are analytic. We also give a description of the set of separatrices of a Newton non-degenerate foliation, which is sufficient to characterize the foliation as Newton non-degenerate when it is of generalized curve type. This allows us to prove that the property of being Newton non-degenerate is topologically invariant for foliations of generalized curve type.
item.dc:creator: Arturo Fern\'andez-P\'erez, Evelia R. Garc\'{i}a Barroso, Rog\'erio Mol

item.title: The closure of the nonreal roots of bounded-height polynomials is connected exactly at pronic heights
item.description: arXiv:2611.14517v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let C_h be the closure of the nonreal roots of integer polynomials with coefficients of modulus at most h. With the nonzero real roots included, the closure is connected at every height; without them, connectedness becomes arithmetic. We prove that C_h is connected exactly when h=q(q-1) is a pronic number 2, 6, 12, 20, ..., and has at least five components otherwise. At height two this confirms a twenty-year-old numerical observation of Shmerkin and Solomyak on double zeros of power series: apart from 1/2 they form the interval $[1/\rho,1)=C_2\cap(0,1)$, with $\rho$ the tribonacci constant. Disconnection is almost always infinite. For (p-1)^2<h<=p^2-3, $h\neq p(p-1)$, infinitely many components with nonempty interior accumulate at $\pm p$ and $\pm 1/p$, and when h<p(p-1) these four points are themselves components. Next to each square q^2>=16, at least two of the three heights q^2-2, q^2-1, q^2 have infinitely many components accumulating at a common point of (1/(q+1),1/q). Explicit series give infinitely many components at every nonpronic height below 167 other than 1, 3, 4, 9, 25, 63 and 81, and in general at most sqrt(X)+1 nonpronic heights h<=X can have finitely many components, although C_h is a Peano compactum at every height. The proofs compare values and derivatives of all admissible power series near a real double zero; the comparison sets are open and closed in the whole core, so components separated near the axis cannot reconnect elsewhere. On the real axis, the double zeros at heights 1, 3, 4, 7 form sets with infinitely many components; at height one this proves a conjecture of Shmerkin and Solomyak and one of Solomyak on the connectedness locus for pairs of affine maps.
item.dc:creator: Bernat Espigule

item.title: A Counterexample to Polynomial Approximation for Monotone Weights
item.description: arXiv:2611.13288v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a counterexample to a question of Borichev on polynomial approximation with monotone weights. We construct an even continuous weight $W$, strictly increasing on $[0,\infty)$, with superpolynomial growth and finite logarithmic integral, and an entire function $F$ of zero exponential type such that $F/W$ vanishes at infinity and belongs to $L^p(\mathbb{R})$ for every $1\leq p<\infty$. Nevertheless, $F$ has positive distance from the polynomials in the weighted uniform norm and in every corresponding weighted $L^{p}$ norm.
item.dc:creator: Natanael Alpay, Paata Ivanisvili

item.title: On Poincar\'e-Type Inequalities for Flags of Distributions
item.description: arXiv:2611.13349v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we establish enumerative formulas and derive geometric inequalities for flags of holomorphic distributions on complex manifolds. First, given a codimension-one holomorphic distribution $\mathcal{G}$ on a complex manifold $M$, we establish an upper bound for the number of independent holomorphic $p$-distributions tangent to $\mathcal{G}$ with a prescribed associated twisting line bundle $\mathcal{L}$. As an application, we prove Poincar\'e-type degree inequalities for flags on certain classes of manifolds. Finally, we investigate the Mumford--Takemoto stability of the tangent sheaves of rank-two distributions. In particular, we establish several stability results for such distributions on projective spaces, smooth weighted complete intersection threefolds, and, in particular, on smooth hypersurfaces $V\subset\mathbb{P}^4$.
item.dc:creator: Antonio M. Ferreira, Miguel Rodr\'iguez Pe\~na, Fernando Louren\c{c}o

item.title: Frames Associated with $C_0$-Semigroups
item.description: arXiv:2611.13867v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A central question in dynamical frame theory asks when the orbit $\{\Lambda^n f\}_{n\in\mathbb{Z}_+}$ of a vector $f$ under a bounded operator $\Lambda$ on a separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space $H$ is a frame. Christensen, Hasannasab and Philipp answered it, showing in particular that such an operator must be similar to the compression of the unilateral shift on $H^2(\mathbb{T})$ to a coinvariant subspace. We prove a continuous analogue: if a $C_0$-semigroup $\{T(t)\}_{t\ge0}\subset B(H)$ generates a continuous frame $\{T(t)\varphi\}_{t\ge0}$, then the operators $T(t)$ are simultaneously similar to the compressions of the shift semigroup to a fixed coinvariant subspace. Moreover, $\{T(t)\varphi\}_{t\ge0}$ is a continuous frame if and only if $\{C^n(I-A)^{-1}\varphi\}_{n\in\mathbb{Z}_+}$ is a frame, where $A$ is the infinitesimal generator and $C=(I+A)(I-A)^{-1}$ the cogenerator; the frame bounds of the two systems differ by a factor $2$. We also derive necessary conditions for the existence of frame vectors and discuss several examples. Finally, we show that the compressed shift on a model space $K_\theta$ is the cogenerator of a $C_0$-semigroup admitting frame vectors if and only if the inner function $\theta$ has a finite angular derivative at $1$; in that case we describe all frame vectors, and the boundary reproducing kernel at $1$ generates a tight continuous frame.
item.dc:creator: Victor Bailey, Eva A. Gallardo-Guti\'errez, Jonathan R. Partington

item.title: Regularity via subequations
item.description: arXiv:2611.14253v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Is there a unified theory of a priori estimates for purely second-order constant coefficient elliptic PDE? A strong indication that such a theory exists is provided by the foundational a priori estimates of Caffarelli--Nirenberg--Spruck (1984) and Trudinger (1995) that treated many equations, yet left out many others. This article develops such a unified theory based on Harvey--Lawson's theory of subequations, the aforementioned a priori estimates, and some new ingredients. Serendipitously, this also solves a problem posed by Nirenberg (2007). In addition to unifying all previously known such estimates, we find a vast number of new a priori estimates (e.g., spanning real, complex, quaternionic, $G_2$, among other natural equations, and even differential inclusions that generalize PDEs).
item.dc:creator: Vasanth Pidaparthy, Yanir A. Rubinstein

item.title: Local Rigidity of Bergman Logarithmic Flatness on Compact Hermitian Symmetric Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.14507v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the local rigidity of Bergman logarithmic flatness near the standard metrics associated with fixed invariant positive polarizations on compact Hermitian symmetric spaces. Every sufficiently small smooth deformation preserving Bergman logarithmic flatness is induced by a holomorphic automorphism and a constant rescaling. This establishes a Bergman analogue of the local rigidity results for Szeg\H{o} logarithmic flatness obtained by Lu--Tian (Duke Math. J., 2004) and, more recently, Loi--Palmieri--Zuddas (2026).
item.dc:creator: Zhiqin Lu, Yuang Shi

item.title: The Bruce-Roberts Tjurina number of holomorphic 1-forms along complex analytic varieties
item.description: arXiv:2409.19814v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce the notion of the \textit{Bruce-Roberts Tjurina number} for holomorphic 1-forms with respect to a pair $(X,V)$ of complex analytic subvarieties. We characterize its finiteness and, when $X$ and $V$ are hypersurfaces with at most isolated singularities, relate it to a determinantal colength, the Tjurina number of the 1-form with respect to $V$, and the Tjurina number of $X$. We also establish a decomposition of the difference between the Bruce-Roberts Milnor and Tjurina numbers and a bound for their quotient. As an application, we prove a relative quasihomogeneity result for germs of non-dicritical generalized curve foliations in complex dimension two.
item.dc:creator: Pedro Barbosa, Arturo Fern\'andez-P\'erez, V\'ictor Le\'on

item.title: Proper maps of annuli
item.description: arXiv:2511.08834v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study proper holomorphic maps of annuli in complex Euclidean spaces, that is, domains with $U(n)$ as the automorphism group. By the Hartogs phenomenon and a result of Forstneri\v{c}, such maps are always rational and extend to proper maps of balls. We first prove that a proper map of annuli from $n$ dimensions to $N$ dimensions where $N < \binom{n+1}{2}$ is always an affine embedding. This inequality is sharp as the homogeneous map of degree 2 satisfies $N=\binom{n+1}{2}$. Next we find a necessary and sufficient condition for a map to be homogeneous: A proper map of annuli is homogeneous if and only if its general hyperplane rank, the affine dimension of the image of a general hyperplane, is exactly $N-1$. As a corollary, we obtain a classification of homogeneous proper maps of balls. A homogeneous proper ball map takes all spheres centered at the origin to spheres centered at the origin. We show that if a proper ball map has general hyperplane rank $N-1$ and takes one sphere centered at the origin to a sphere centered at the origin, then it is homogeneous. Another corollary of this result is a complete classification of proper maps of annuli from dimension 2 to dimension 3. Finally, we give a complete normal form of rational proper maps of annuli of degree 2.
item.dc:creator: Abdullah Al Helal, Jiri Lebl, Achinta Kumar Nandi

item.title: Analytic multiplier ideals of toric plurisubharmonic functions on a toric complex space
item.description: arXiv:2610.08741v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study analytic multiplier ideal sheaves of toric plurisubharmonic functions on normal affine toric complex analytic spaces equipped with torus-invariant rational divisors, assuming that a positive integer multiple of the log canonical divisor is Cartier. We describe these sheaves in terms of Newton convex bodies and show that they are globally generated by finitely many meromorphic monomials. Our results generalize the description of An and the formulas of Howald and Blickle for monomial ideals, and recover the descriptions of Rashkovskii and Guenancia on affine space. We also extend this description to weights obtained by subtracting positive rational multiples of monomial ideal weights.
item.dc:creator: Hoseob Seo

item.title: A Dynamical Fekete-Szeg\H{o} Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2603.01684v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $E\subset\mathbb{C}$ be a compact set, symmetric with respect to the real axis and regular for the Dirichlet problem. A classical theorem of Fekete and Szeg\H{o} asserts that if $cap(E)\ge 1$ then every neighbourhood of $E$ contains infinitely many complete sets of conjugate algebraic integers. We prove a dynamical strengthening: $cap(E)\ge1$ if and only if every neighbourhood of the polynomially convex hull $Pc(E)$ contains filled Julia sets of monic integral polynomials of arbitrarily large degree. When $cap(E)=1$, we show that the minimal polynomials $P_n$ of distinct algebraic integers whose entire Galois orbits approach $E$ have filled Julia sets $K_{P_n}$ converging to $Pc(E)$ in the Klimek metric, and Brolin measures converging to the equilibrium measure $\mu_E$. The key step is that algebraic numbers of small Rumely height $h_E$ have minimal polynomials that are asymptotically minimal on $E$. As an arithmetic application, we show that the Call--Silverman canonical heights $\hat{h}_{P_n}$ converge to $h_E$ uniformly on $\bar{\mathbb{Q}}$.
item.dc:creator: Turgay Bayraktar, Melike Efe

item.title: Stacky geometry and logarithmic topology of transversely affine foliations
item.description: arXiv:2605.27669v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the linear monodromy of codimension-one transversely affine foliations through multiplicative quotient stacks and logarithmic boundary topology. When the transverse affine structure admits a global presentation on $U$, a choice of multiplicative developing coordinate induces a morphism to $[\mathbb{C}^*/\Gamma]$, where $\Gamma\subset\mathbb{C}^*$ is the image of the linear monodromy. We prove that for infinite $\Gamma$ every strict semi-equivariant holomorphic self-map of $\mathbb{C}^*$ is a monomial, and classify the nonconstant strict semi-equivariant rational self-maps of $\mathbb{P}^1$ for arbitrary $\Gamma$. For a logarithmic connection along a simple normal crossings divisor, we describe the meridional characters and angular foliations on the boundary fibres of the Kato--Nakayama space, including the topology and closures of their leaves. We also describe the extension of the linear monodromy local system to this space and the effect of local Kummer base change on finite meridional monodromy.
item.dc:creator: Pedro Barbassa, Gabriel Santos Barbosa, Maur\'icio Corr\^ea

item.title: Impulse Response Estimation via Laguerre-Fourier Expansion
item.description: arXiv:2608.14769v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The empirical transfer function estimate (ETFE) is a widely used method for system identification of linear time-invariant (LTI) systems in engineering disciplines such as acoustics, audio engineering, seismography, and tomography. However, ETFE suffers from numerical limitations when the excitation signal is band-limited or vanishes at certain frequencies, which is a common physical constraint of the excitation in practice. In such cases, division in the frequency domain becomes heavily ill-conditioned, and small measurement disturbances or numerical inaccuracies can degrade the solution. This paper presents L-ETFE, a generalization of ETFE based on Laguerre-Fourier expansions that addresses these limitations. After a suitable transformation, the method can yield a well-conditioned circulant problem even when the original ETFE system is ill-conditioned. Solving this problem via classical ETFE yields the discrete Laguerre-Fourier coefficients of the system's transfer function. The desired impulse response (IR) of the system-to-be-identified can then be recovered by a subsequent transformation pipeline. We derive novel and efficient algorithms for performing these transformations and analyse the conditioning of the transformed problem, explicitly characterizing its dependence on the input and a parameter used in the Laguerre-Fourier expansion. We evaluate the method on two simulated discrete-time LTI systems of varying complexity. The experiments demonstrate accurate IR recovery for spectral-zero and band-limited excitation, where standard ETFE fails.
item.dc:creator: Tam\'as D\'ozsa, Art J. R. Pelling, Matthias Voigt

item.title: Characterizations of Toeplitz operators on the annulus
item.description: arXiv:2610.40118v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish algebraic characterizations of Toeplitz operators on the Hardy space on the annulus. As an application, we characterize compact perturbations of Toeplitz operators and prove a zero-product result.
item.dc:creator: Sayan Adhikari, Susmita Das, Shubham Jain, Jaydeb Sarkar

item.title: A general framework for universal bounds on the analytic functional calculus
item.description: arXiv:2611.01503v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish a general principle for bounding the matrix-valued analytic functional calculus $F\mapsto F(T)$ of a Hilbert space operator $T$, independently of the matrix size. It rests on two properties of an auxiliary Hilbert space of holomorphic functions: the accretivity of its moment map at $T$ and a uniform bound for its multipliers. The mechanism of OpenAI's direct proof of the complete Crouzeix conjecture is the instance in which these properties come from the positivity of the double-layer potential and from norm estimates for Faber series of a convex domain. The main advantage of our method is that the auxiliary space can be chosen freely, to fit the class of operators, and a well-chosen space can give sharp constants, also on domains that are not convex, simply connected or bounded. On every intersection of two disks of the Riemann sphere, for operators with both closed disks as spectral sets, we obtain the complete bound $2$, which is sharp for the quantum annulus and the strip. For operators, bounded or m-sectorial, with numerical range in a sector, our bounds improve on the complete Crouzeix inequality for every opening; they are optimal for the right angle, answering a question of Crouzeix, and nearly optimal for acute angles. On Jordan domains with regular real-analytic boundary, a space built from the exterior conformal map and the Faber polynomials of the domain gives complete bounds for operators whose double-layer potential is bounded below. They are optimal for the disk, recover the complete Crouzeix inequality on convex domains, and improve on earlier bounds, including bounds of Crouzeix and Greenbaum, also on nonconvex domains.
item.dc:creator: Mihai Putinar, Georgios Tsikalas
